title: A French prize will publish fiction co-written with an AI model
friendlyTitle: A French prize will publish fiction written with an AI model
summary: The Guardian reports that the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA is open for unpublished fiction co-written with a language model. Entries must be 10,000 to 50,000 words, in French, and must name the model and the prompt. Entrants can be anywhere. The terms also ask that the text help address an ethical, social, or ecological problem. The winner is promised publication. Applications close at the end of November, a shortlist of 10 follows, and the winner is due in early December. Submissions go through prixpascal.fr. The prize was founded by technology entrepreneurs Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant, and Gilles Mentré.

whyItMatters: If you write with a model, this is a rare contest that asks you to disclose that, instead of treating it as something to hide. The constraints are real: French, a word range, an unpublished manuscript, and a stated problem the text is meant to address. Disclosure of the prompt is part of the entry, not an optional note.
